name: Modular Monolith Design
tagline: Structuring a single deployable binary into isolated vertical domain modules with enforced APIs and private schemas.
purpose: Achieve clean domain boundaries, ~50 ns in-process calls, and single-DB ACID transactions without jumping prematurely to microservices.

spark.summary: Structure a single deployable binary into strictly isolated domain modules with enforced public APIs and private schemas—gaining clean boundaries without network tax.
spark.keyTakeaway: Enforce module boundaries at compile/test time (ArchUnit, Spring Modulith, import-linter) and isolate database schemas so any module can be extracted into a microservice in days when scale demands it.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **modular monolith** packages multiple cohesive **vertical business modules** (`orders`, `inventory`, `billing`) inside one deployable process—never sliced by technical layer (`controllers`, `services`, `repositories`).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Public Facade + Async Domain Events Between Vertical Modules (Orders Module -> Inventory Public API -> Inventory Internal -> In-Process Outbox); Modular Monolith -> Async Module Events -> Extracted Service (VERTICAL SLICE -> ASYNC EVENTS -> MICROSERVICE).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare coupling, transaction support, and deployment independence. Explore Outbox CDC, microservices decomposition, Hexagonal Architecture, and Strangler Fig.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore Outbox CDC, microservices decomposition, Hexagonal Architecture, and Strangler Fig.

learningJourney.title: What is a Modular Monolith
learningJourney.explanation:
A **modular monolith** packages multiple cohesive **vertical business modules** (`orders`, `inventory`, `billing`) inside one deployable process—never sliced by technical layer (`controllers`, `services`, `repositories`).

Each module exposes a narrow **public API** (facade + DTOs + domain events) while keeping its entities, repositories, and database tables strictly private.

sectionDiagram.title: Public Facade + Async Domain Events Between Vertical Modules
sectionDiagram.summary: Orders never imports Inventory's internal ORM entities or runs SQL JOINs against inventory tables.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how a Modular Monolith works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why teams fall into Big Balls of Mud—or premature microservices
learningJourney.explanation:
Jumping straight from a tangled monolith to microservices trades code coupling for distributed systems complexity (network latency, Sagas, service mesh).

Yet modular monoliths fail if boundaries are merely cultural: **Boundary Erosion** (a developer imports another module's internal entity under deadline pressure) and **Database-Level Coupling** (cross-module SQL `JOIN`s) silently turn the codebase back into a Big Ball of Mud.

ideas.title: Automated CI Fitness Functions
ideas.description: Fail the build automatically on illegal cross-module imports using ArchUnit (Java), Spring Modulith, Packwerk (Ruby), or `import-linter` (Python).

ideas.title: Separate PostgreSQL Schemas
ideas.description: Give each module its own DB schema (`orders.*`, `billing.*`) with least-privilege roles or schema-prefix linting.

learningJourney.title: Where Modular Monoliths excel (and when to extract)
learningJourney.explanation: Start with a modular monolith for most products; extract only when hardware, scale, or compliance forces process separation.

benefits: ~50 ns in-process calls, single-DB ACID transactions, and one CI/CD pipeline while boundaries stabilize.
costs: Shared runtime blast radius (one OOM kills the process).

comparison.choice: Avoid: Incompatible Runtimes or Strict Isolation
benefits: Extract Python/PyTorch GPU inference, Rust proxies, or PCI-DSS cardholder vaults into separate services.
costs: Co-locating incompatible runtimes or compliance scopes in one process creates operational risk.

learningJourney.title: Enforcing Module Boundaries with ArchUnit / Spring Modulith
learningJourney.explanation: Encode module encapsulation as a unit test in CI so illegal internal imports fail PRs immediately.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Layered Monolith vs. Modular Monolith vs. Microservices
learningJourney.explanation: Compare coupling, transaction support, and deployment independence.

benefits: Clean vertical slices, zero network tax, single ACID DB, easy future extraction.
costs: Coupled scaling and shared process blast radius.

benefits: Independent scaling, fault isolation, and polyglot runtimes.
costs: 2–10 ms network hops, Sagas, distributed tracing, and mesh overhead.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: In-Process Eventual Consistency for Zero-Friction Extraction
learningJourney.explanation: If Module A relies heavily on synchronous cross-module ACID transactions with Module B, extracting Module B later still requires rewriting those writes into Sagas. Using **in-process domain events + module-private tables** today makes extracting a module into a standalone service take days.

sectionDiagram.title: Modular Monolith -> Async Module Events -> Extracted Service
sectionDiagram.summary: Decoupling via private schemas and async events inside the monolith is the cheapest path to future microservices.

options.text: Organize packages by technical layer (controllers, services, repositories)
options.feedback: Technical-layer packaging encourages cross-domain entanglement; organize by vertical business capability instead.

options.text: Enforce vertical module boundaries in CI (ArchUnit / import-linter) and isolate database tables per module schema
options.feedback: Correct: automated CI fitness functions and schema isolation stop boundary erosion before code merges.

options.text: Allow any module to run SQL JOINs across all tables for convenience
options.feedback: Cross-module SQL JOINs couple schemas together and block future extraction.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** A **modular monolith** packages multiple cohesive **vertical business modules** (`orders`, `inventory`, `billing`) inside one deployable process—never sliced by technical layer (`controllers`, `services`, `repositories`).

**How It Flows:** Think of Modular Monolith Design as a clear step-by-step chain: Orders Module -> Inventory Public API -> Inventory Internal -> In-Process Outbox -> VERTICAL SLICE.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Enforce module boundaries at compile/test time (ArchUnit, Spring Modulith, import-linter) and isolate database schemas so any module can be extracted into a microservice in days when scale demands it.
